name: Greco-Persian Wars
description: The Achaemenid Empire's attempts to subdue the Greek city-states, turned back at Marathon, Salamis, and Plataea. Victory preserved Greek political independence and launched Athens' imperial golden age.

name: Peloponnesian War
description: The ruinous struggle between Athens' naval empire and Sparta's land alliance, chronicled by Thucydides as a study in power politics. Plague, the Sicilian disaster, and Persian gold brought Athens down — and exhausted Greece for Macedon's taking.

name: Punic Wars
description: Three wars between Rome and Carthage for the western Mediterranean — including Hannibal's Alpine invasion and Cannae, Rome's darkest defeat — ending with Carthage razed and Rome the unrivalled Mediterranean power.

name: The Crusades
description: Two centuries of papally sanctioned expeditions to the Levant, from the First Crusade's capture of Jerusalem to the fall of Acre. They built and lost crusader states, sacked Christian Constantinople in 1204, and left durable marks on trade, memory, and Christian-Muslim relations.

name: Hundred Years' War
description: The dynastic struggle between England and France — Crécy, Poitiers, Agincourt, Joan of Arc — that forged both national identities, ended chivalric cavalry dominance with the longbow and cannon, and expelled England from France save Calais.

name: Thirty Years' War
description: Europe's most destructive religious-political war, fought largely on German soil where perhaps a third of the population died. Ended at Westphalia with the state system that still frames international relations.

name: Seven Years' War
description: Arguably the first world war, fought in Europe, North America, the Caribbean, West Africa, and India. Britain emerged the dominant colonial and naval power — with debts whose taxation of America sparked revolution.

name: Napoleonic Wars
description: France's bid for European hegemony under Napoleon: mass conscript armies, the Continental System, the catastrophic Russian campaign, and final defeat at Waterloo — settled at Vienna into a century's balance of power.

name: American Civil War
description: The Union's war against the secessionist slaveholding Confederacy — the first great industrial war of railways, telegraphs, ironclads, and trenches — killing some 750,000 and ending American slavery.

name: First World War
description: Industrialized attrition on continental scale: trenches from the Channel to Switzerland, artillery, gas, and roughly seventeen million dead. Four empires collapsed, the map of Europe and the Middle East was redrawn, and the unresolved peace incubated the next war.

name: Second World War
description: The deadliest conflict in history — perhaps seventy million dead — spanning Europe, Asia, Africa, and every ocean, encompassing the Holocaust's industrial genocide and ending with atomic bombs, a divided Europe, and the United Nations.

name: Vietnam War
description: The Cold War's longest proxy conflict: North Vietnam and the Viet Cong against South Vietnam and the United States. Guerrilla warfare, mass bombing, and televised carnage broke American consensus; Saigon fell in 1975.
